fields.description:
Surfaced by the comment triage, and it is a live contract defect rather than a comment problem.

`_mcp_models.py` hand-mirrors five committed JSON schemas as pydantic models, each with an explicit
"Mirrors src/rebar/schemas/<name>.schema.json" comment and no generator or drift gate.

**The drift is real and shipped.** `BridgeFsckOut` (`_mcp_models.py:185`) declares three properties;
`bridge_fsck.schema.json` has four — `binding_drift` is missing. `_engine_support/bridge_fsck.py:217`
emits it unconditionally, and the generated `types.py:311` has it. So the MCP `outputSchema`
advertised to clients under-declares a field the tool always returns.

**And the comment that should have caught it asserts an enforcement that does not exist.**
`_mcp_models.py:31-34` claims "the cross-interface schema tests pin both to the canonical schema" —
but `rg BridgeFsckOut|GroundingInfoOut|WorkflowRunOut tests/` returns ZERO hits. No test pins these
three. That false assurance is precisely why the drift went unnoticed.

A second drift found in the same sweep: `VerifySignatureResultOut` (`:210`) makes `algorithm`,
`head_sha` and `key_id` optional while the schema requires all three.

The sibling TypedDict layer already has the fix pattern: `schemas/gen_types.py` generates it and CI
enforces currency via `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types --check`
(`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:545`). The MCP model layer — the other consumer of the same
schemas — has no equivalent.

Extending the generator to cover `_mcp_models.py` closes the drift class permanently and deletes
the five "Mirrors ..." comments as a side effect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `BridgeFsckOut` declares `binding_drift`
- [x] `VerifySignatureResultOut`'s required set matches its schema
- [x] The MCP model layer is generated from the schemas, or covered by an equivalent `--check` drift gate
- [x] The false "cross-interface schema tests pin both" comment is removed or made true
- [x] The five hand-sync "Mirrors ..." comments are gone
